public_rationale: Google's own May 30, 2024 post admits that odd and inaccurate AI Overviews showed up after the launch. It confirms the rocks and glue-on-pizza answers and lists more than a dozen fixes. The AP reported that while many examples were silly, others were dangerous. A Purdue mycologist said an AI Overview on which wild mushrooms to eat left out information that could be 'sickening or even fatal.' That covers both ends of his range, from hilarious to dangerous. Google says some dangerous-looking screenshots were fakes, and that policy violations were rare. But real dangerous answers were documented, and the launch forced public fixes. That fits a plain reading of 'disastrous launch'.
limitations: 'Disastrous' is a judgment; it is assessed here by the public failures and forced fixes, not by any usage metric.
Some viral dangerous examples were reportedly fake, so the dangerous part rests on a smaller set of verified cases.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Google's AI-powered search summaries had a disastrous launch, producing results ranging from hilarious to actively life-threatening.

statement.excerpt: Results are filled with Search Engine Optimized spam, ads and sponsored content are bordering on indistinguishable from regular results, and the disastrous launch of Google's AI-powered "summaries" produced results that ranged from hilarious to actively life-threatening.

from_speaker: produced results that ranged from hilarious to actively life-threatening
our_interpretation: The 'summaries' are Google's AI Overviews, which rolled out to all US users in mid-May 2024.

Plain reading: around the launch, AI Overviews produced widely reported absurd answers and also some answers that could put a user in real danger if followed, and Google had to respond with fixes. 'Disastrous' is a characterization; it is read as a launch with widely publicized failures that forced public corrections.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous reporting or Google's own statements show that AI Overviews at launch produced absurd answers (such as eating rocks or glue on pizza) and at least some answers that experts judged dangerous, and that Google had to make corrections.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence that the viral absurd or dangerous answers were not real AI Overviews, or that the launch went without notable public failures.
